records.central_bank: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan)
records.category: suspected graft referred against an official of a central bank subsidiary; no case opened and no prosecution
records.people: an anonymised former deputy director of the Central Mint (named only as 'A jun' in the published report); the Central Mint of China, a Central Bank of the Republic of China subsidiary; the Central Bank's own ethics office; the Ministry of Justice Agency Against Corruption; the Taipei District Prosecutors Office
records.summary: The Control Yuan's published investigation report on the Central Mint of China, a subsidiary of Taiwan's central bank, records that after the central bank found a power cable running from a plant socket to the private car of the Mint's deputy director during a routine property check, the Mint's own ethics office judged that criminal liability might be involved and that the conduct might amount to graft, and referred the case through the Central Bank's ethics office to the Ministry of Justice Agency Against Corruption. The report states that the Agency Against Corruption judged that the matter involved no official-duty conduct and no offence of graft, so it opened no investigation and returned the case to the Central Bank's ethics office to be handled as an ordinary unlawful-act matter, and that the Taipei District Prosecutors Office issued a decision not to prosecute the electricity-theft offence the official had reported himself for, on the ground of insufficient suspicion.
records.detail: A second and separate Taiwanese episode from the one the map holds, which is the 2019 Mirror Media report of questioned procurement at the Central Engraving and Printing Plant, a different subsidiary, with different actors and a different year. Dates on the source page are written in the Republic of China calendar, and the conversions given here are arithmetic on those printed values and nothing more: the property check is dated 111 nian 8 yue 11 ri (11 August 2022), the two-demerit penalty 111 nian 8 yue 31 ri (31 August 2022), the Central Bank's dismissal of the official's administrative appeal 112 nian 11 yue 6 ri (6 November 2023), and the prosecutors' non-prosecution decision 113 nian 5 yue 13 ri (13 May 2024). The source_url serves a Microsoft Word document rather than a PDF, which is how the Control Yuan publishes the public version of this report; a date-checking script fetching it must read it as a .docx. Two further Control Yuan documents on the same matter were downloaded and read and are named here as second sources: the corrective-measure text against the Central Mint, 114 cai zheng 2, at https://multimedia.cy.gov.tw/DocFiles/IFDEWebBBS_CY/Docs/114/3RD/00/37/Attach/114caizheng2-gonggao-v1.docx (the live path uses backslashes and the Chinese characters cai zheng), which corrects the Mint for failing to investigate a workplace-bullying complaint under the Occupational Safety and Health Act and the Ministry of Labor's guidance revised on 111 nian 8 yue 18 ri (18 August 2022) and calls the handling a clear dereliction; and the Finance and Economics Committee's closure table at https://cybsbox.cy.gov.tw/CYBSBoxSSL/edoc/download/72060, which records the Central Bank stating that the Mint's handling of the complaint left room for improvement and the committee resolving on 114.06.04 (4 June 2025) to close the corrective case. Only the graft referral and its closure are filed as the case here; the bullying-handling dereliction is an official finding against the subsidiary but is not corruption, so it is reported in notes rather than filed as a case.
records.quote: 法務部廉政署判斷本件未涉職務行為，亦非涉貪瀆罪名
records.source_title: Control Yuan of the Republic of China, published investigation report on the Central Mint of China (public version), case on the penalising of an employee and the handling of his complaint
